newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers ease off from earlier highs.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers ease off from earlier highs.

text.p: North American bunker prices mostly eased down on Thursday from high numbers reached on Tuesday after the U.S. fired retaliatory missiles at Iraq, traders said.
"The Iraq crisis drove prices up on Tuesday, but there was not much demand to support them so they have started to come off," said one West Coast trader.
In Los Angeles, 380 CST was slightly weaker in very thin activity, trading between $102 and $103 a tonne, with 180 CST at $104/105, players said.
In New York Harbor, 380 CST edged down $4 to $108/109 and Norfolk hub dipped only a $1 due to the port's major supplier being temporarily out of fuel.
On the Gulf Coast, however, Houston 380 CST rose $1 to $105/106, as did 180 CST, due to tight avails of higher grades of bunkers.
Traders said suppliers were reluctant to restock because prices are still at higher numbers prior to the U.S. military action against Iraq on Tuesday.
"People are worried about covering supplies at these levels in case the market comes down further," said one Gulf Coast trader.
Players said firmer NYMEX crude oil and heating oil futures, however, may underpin strength in the market.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
